counterexamples.statement: Histories [supply <>] and [supply <>, admit d, admit s] have the same supply subsequence; the first has no coproduct structure, the second has it (tokens d, s classified Difference, Structure).

counterexamples.rationale: Claim a history of mentions alone leaves the empty state; here all but one nonempty supply-only history is said to move it (inertness is the L1 rule).
Claim every history that inscribes <> reaches coproduct structure, i.e. read the inscription as the root Real_0 = Difference + Structure.
Claim coproduct structure needs a supply of <>; the unrooted model reaches it by admitting two channel data alone (the Rust replay then refuses such a history for lacking the root event).
Claim admitting <> itself already yields both channels; one admitted token carries one class.
Claim an extra leading mention of <> changes the outcome for many histories; under the model rule it changes none.
Claim a leading mention of <> is inert under every step rule because of how it is spelled; under the rival rule (supply admits) it changes the outcome.
Ignore the requirement that the first event be the supply of <>: count every unrefused history as rooted.
Count states as if re-admission of an admitted datum duplicated it (law L6 chooses designation), inflating the reachable states.
Claim the leading supply of <> is invisible to the rooted outcome; omitting it turns an accepted history into a refusal (MissingLiteralRoot), so it is an admission precondition, not inert.
Claim every history accepted by the unrooted model is accepted by the rooted replay; the rooted gate refuses all histories not beginning with the supply of <>, including the empty one.
Claim that supplies after the root can change the rooted outcome; only the first supply is a precondition, later ones are inert.

claim_boundary.supports: The node is a DEFINITION, so the result is a consistency and independence result for it, not a proof of it. In a three-event finite admission model (supply, admit datum, admit form) in which supply is STIPULATED to be the identity on the admitted state, the kernel proves (lean4/InertDiamond.lean, over any token type with decidable equality): in the UNROOTED replay, deleting every supply event changes no outcome or refusal, so any function of the outcome is independent of how many times, or where, <> (or any token) is mentioned; in the ROOTED replay (the model of the Rust gate: the first event must be the supply of <>) the FIRST supply is an admission precondition (omitting it from an accepted history is refused) and every later supply is inert; only admission-class events can change the state, and admitting a not-yet-admitted token does; a history that only supplies and admits <> never satisfies the model predicate HasCoproduct (an admitted Difference-classified datum and an admitted Structure-classified datum) for ANY classification of tokens (Lean statement; the native replay uses one fixed classification); the predicate HasCoproduct is independent of inscribing <> (same supply subsequence, one history without and one with two admitted channel data); the identification Real_0 = Difference join Structure is NOT modelled; "coproduct predicate without any supply of <>" is realised only in the UNROOTED model (the rooted replay refuses it for lacking the root event), so in the rooted model inscription is necessary and only its non-sufficiency is shown; and inertness is a rule of the step function, not of the spelling: a rival rule under which supply admits is exhibited. Exhaustive native replay of all 8-event traces of length <= 5 (37449 traces), with a rooted-replay column set (later supplies change the rooted outcome in 0 traces; omitting the root supply is refused for 1, 7, 49, 343, 2401 histories at lengths 1 to 5; the rooted gate refuses 7, 49, ... histories the unrooted model accepts). The zero native counts of supply-deletion and prefix-mention differences follow from supply being the identity by definition and corroborate the implementation, not the inertness hypothesis. The correspondence of the model rules (supply is the identity, arity 0 refused, re-admission designates) to the Rust admission step rests on reading omega_ooutwire_primitives/src/admission.rs, which is not among the run inputs; the gate on the first event is read from genesis_construction.rs line 174.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: The identification Real_0 = Difference joined with Structure (it is not modelled; only a stand-in predicate is shown independent of the inscription); the remaining three events of the six-operation alphabet (instance, rule, imposition) and their refusal rules; the Rust partial admission rules beyond the three-event fragment; any claim that supply is inert independently of the stipulated step rule; inertness of the FIRST supply in the rooted replay; any physical or interpretive reading of <>.
